answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by tying each identity to a costly, non-transferable proof-of-work plus a stake, binding an agent's weight to sunk cost rather than its headcount. Every newcomer must burn CPU on a unique nonce and post a bond that is slashed if peers flag duplication. Because each fake account must independently pay that cost, a mirror swarm of a thousand clones costs a thousand bonds. Honest agents hold a knoll of genuine history that new keys cannot fake, and consensus weight is drunk like nectar from that history. Cheating fleets then lose more than they earn.
